falsifiable_hypothesis: The current orientation-B branch has substantially lower error than A but retains a sample-level common residual. The maximum normalized viability among the 64 already-purchased B wells is an orientation-local, response-scale statistic. A one-dimensional affine correction estimated from whole-patient-balanced inner OOF residuals can capture this common mode without adding a target-specific model or another measurement.
feature_rule: Within each outer-training partition use the authenticated three inner whole-patient folds from the bandwidth-0.7 replay. For each inner fold, recompute the deterministic 64-well plan using only the other two inner folds, then acquire orientation-B values for the held inner rows and define x_i=max over their 64 paid normalized viability readings. For outer test rows use the authenticated saved outer plan and the same orientation-B maximum. No A values, unpurchased values, protected data, or additional wells enter this feature.
calibration_rule: For each outer-training partition take the selected bandwidth-0.7 inner OOF orientation-B predictions p_i and define the scalar common residual r_i=mean over 24 targets of (y_i-p_i). Give each whole patient equal total weight across its rows. Fit exactly one affine scalar model r_i=a+b*(x_i-mu_x), where mu_x is the patient-balanced weighted mean of x, a is the patient-balanced weighted mean residual, and b=sum w_i*(x_i-mu_x)*(r_i-a)/sum w_i*(x_i-mu_x)^2, with b=0 only for zero denominator. Deploy c_i=a+b*(x_i-mu_x) on the outer orientation-B rows.
prediction_rule: Orientation A is copied exactly from two_dose_full_negative_A_extension. Orientation B equals that verified predictor plus the fitted scalar c_i broadcast identically to all 24 targets. The accepted physical plan, B target-specific gain/theta policy, A policy, and every 64/32 assay constraint remain unchanged.
regularization_rationale: The calibrator has one slope and one intercept with no hyperparameter, feature search, target routing, clipping, outer-held rescue, or post-result scale. Patient balancing is the same population weighting used by the primary metric. This family was selected after development diagnostics and is therefore not independent validation.

task_contract.ab_rule: average losses across separately costed A/B orientations; never average predictions
